## What we make
Tennis ball cricket bats for street, gully and club cricket — not leather-ball
bats. Six profiles: standard, scoop, flat, big edge, mongoose, and double or
triple blade. 29 models.

## Guides
- [Which bat should you use for tennis ball cricket?](https://tossports.in/guides/which-bat-for-tennis-ball-cricket/): Use a lighter Poplar or Kashmir Willow bat for the soft tennis ball, and a heavier, harder-pressed Sri Lankan wood bat for the medium or hard tennis ball. Playing a soft-ball bat against a hard ball is the single most common reason a tennis bat cracks within a season.
- [What weight bat should you use?](https://tossports.in/guides/what-weight-cricket-bat-should-i-use/): For tennis ball cricket, most adults are best served between 750g and 850g. Go under 750g if you rely on timing and play square of the wicket; go over 850g only if you genuinely clear the rope and can still swing it late in an innings.
- [Scoop, flat or big edge — which profile?](https://tossports.in/guides/scoop-vs-flat-vs-big-edge-bat/): A scoop removes wood from the back so the bat swings faster at the same weight; a big edge adds wood to the sides so there is more bat behind a mishit; a flat bat gives the largest hitting face for tennis ball cricket. Choose scoop for hand speed, big edge for power, flat for a big margin of error.
- [Looking after a tennis ball cricket bat](https://tossports.in/guides/how-to-care-for-tennis-ball-bat/): Tennis ball cricket bats do not need knocking in. Keep the bat dry, tape the toe before it frays, and never use it on a wet ground or against a leather ball — those three habits are worth more than any oiling routine.
- [Sri Lankan wood, Kashmir Willow or Poplar?](https://tossports.in/guides/sri-lankan-vs-kashmir-willow-vs-poplar/): Sri Lankan (Ceylon) wood is the densest of the three and best for the hard tennis ball; Kashmir Willow is lighter with better pickup for the soft ball; Poplar is the most affordable and suits beginners and younger players. For most Chennai club cricket, Sri Lankan wood is the right answer.
- [Buying a cricket bat in Chennai](https://tossports.in/guides/buy-cricket-bat-chennai/): You can buy directly from our workshop at Nesapakkam, Chennai, or from Toss The Turf in Kolathur. Bats run from ₹950 to ₹2,999, we cut to your weight, and you can message us on WhatsApp before paying anything.
- [Wooden or plastic cricket bat?](https://tossports.in/guides/wooden-vs-plastic-cricket-bat/): Buy a wooden bat if you play regularly with a tennis ball — it hits further, lasts seasons, and can be cut to your weight. Plastic bats only make sense for children under ten, for the beach, or for a one-off game where the bat will be abused and abandoned.
